key_insight: Cova-PINN improves fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer prediction by enforcing conservation across thermal interaction paths, not just within separately sampled fluid and solid domains.
engineering_relevance: The method is especially relevant for heat exchangers and other complex geometries where accurate outlet temperature and end-to-end energy balance matter more than visually plausible temperature fields.
method: Cross-domain composite control-volume balances are optimized at the local scale.
Paired-wall closure is enforced at the global exchanger scale.
Multi-domain PINN supports medium-specific representations while aligning conservation with heat-transfer pathways.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on four TPMS heat exchangers and a DualMS design, Cova-PINN outperformed baselines under a common protocol, reducing average outlet-temperature and device-level closure errors by 37.7% and 60.2% versus the closest baseline.
watch_item: The approach adds conservation constraints tied to geometry and wall pairing, so performance may depend on correct path definitions and careful formulation for new exchanger layouts.
paper_title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
